frames.narration: A service reports that customer acme used 12 gigabyte-hours of storage between 14:00 and 14:05. The event carries an id made by the service, e-7731, the customer, the metric, the quantity and the time it happened.
The ingest API appends the event to the log, in the partition for acme, and only then says it is accepted. The service now knows the event is safe.
The deduplicator reads the event and checks the id store. It has not seen e-7731, so it remembers the id and passes the event on. The event goes to the archive too.
The 14:00 hourly window for acme and this metric held 988 units. The aggregator adds 12 by event time, and the window now holds 1,000.
The service did not see the answer in time and sends e-7731 again. The log delivers it a second time, but the id is already remembered, so the deduplicator drops it. The window stays at 1,000.

At the end of the month acme has 1,200 units of this metric. The invoice engine prices them with the plan in force: the first 1,000 at 10 cents is 100.00 and the next 200 at 8 cents is 16.00, so the invoice line is 116.00.
Two days later a service that was offline reports 4 more units from the last week of the month. The window is closed, so the usage store records a correction, and the event is archived.

The next invoice gets an adjustment line. The total for 1,204 units is 100.00 plus 204 at 8 cents, which is 116.32. Since 116.00 was already billed, the adjustment is 0.32, and the customer can see the event behind it.
